screening_decisions.reason: RCT in women with SUI/MUI comparing PFM training vs untreated control group (no contact during intervention). Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, women with UI, PFMT arm, and inactive control.

Study protocol for RCT comparing nurse specialist involvement vs usual care. Does not specifically test PFMT - intervention is care pathway modification, not PFMT. Control is usual care, not inactive control.
RCT assessing satisfaction with nurse specialist care vs GP care. Does not test PFMT as intervention - focuses on care delivery model. Control is usual GP care, not inactive control.

RCT in women with urge/mixed UI. Behavioral training (with/without biofeedback) includes PFMT components. Self-help booklet serves as inactive control. Meets criteria with PFMT/behavioral intervention vs inactive control.
Feasibility study, not RCT. Although it includes PFMT, study design does not meet RCT criterion for this review.
RCT comparing two PFMT delivery methods (supervised vs unsupervised). Both arms are active PFMT interventions - no inactive control arm (no treatment/placebo/sham).
RCT in women with SUI and LBP. Control group received routine physiotherapy modalities and regular exercises - active treatment, not inactive control. Does not meet criteria for inactive control arm.
RCT in women with stress/mixed UI. Behavioral training (includes PFMT) compared to self-help booklet (inactive control). Meets criteria with PFMT/behavioral intervention vs inactive control arm.

RCT in elderly women with UI. Training group included Kegel's exercises (PFMT). Control group mentioned but details unclear. Includes PFMT component with control comparison - conservative decision to include.
RCT in women with UI. Behavioral therapy intervention (typically includes PFMT) compared to no therapy (inactive control). Meets criteria for PFMT/behavioral intervention vs inactive control.

Economic evaluation alongside RCT comparing two PFMT delivery methods (Internet vs postal). Both arms are active PFMT - no inactive control arm. Focus is on cost-effectiveness, not PFMT vs inactive control.
RCT comparing two PFMT delivery methods (Internet vs postal). Both arms are active PFMT interventions - no inactive control arm. Does not meet criteria for inactive control comparison.
Long-term follow-up of RCT comparing two PFMT delivery methods (Internet vs postal). Both arms are active PFMT - no inactive control arm. Does not meet criteria for inactive control comparison.

RCT in women with SUI. Intervention includes PFMT (co-contraction of TA and PFM). Control group present (though details unclear). Includes PFMT component with control - conservative decision to include.

Pilot RCT in frail women with UI. Behavioral UI treatments (likely includes PFMT) combined with physical activity. Control group present. Behavioral treatments for UI typically include PFMT - conservative decision to include.

RCT in gynecological cancer survivors with pelvic floor dysfunction, not specifically UI. Control received usual health care (active treatment, not inactive control). Population and control do not meet criteria.
Questionnaire validation study, not RCT. Focuses on psychometric properties of ICIQ instrument. Does not meet RCT criterion.
Systematic review, not primary RCT. Reviews other RCTs but is not itself an RCT. Does not meet RCT criterion.
Systematic review, not primary RCT. Reviews other RCTs but is not itself an RCT. Does not meet RCT criterion.
Methodology/guideline paper about CONSORT statement extension, not RCT. Does not meet RCT criterion.
Review/opinion paper discussing impact of UI on quality of life, not RCT. Does not meet RCT criterion.
Psychometric validation study of I-QOL questionnaire, not RCT. Focuses on cross-cultural performance of measurement tool. Does not meet RCT criterion.
Instrument validation study testing reproducibility of measurement tools, not RCT. Does not meet RCT criterion.
Observational imaging study using MRI to assess pelvic floor muscle function, not RCT. Does not meet RCT criterion.
Discussion/review paper theorizing about mechanisms of PFMT effectiveness, not RCT. Does not meet RCT criterion.

This is a consensus-based terminology report, not a randomised or quasi-randomised controlled trial. It describes development of definitions through expert consensus and review processes, with no intervention arms or randomisation.
This is a cross-sectional Internet survey (EpiLUTS), not a randomised controlled trial. It examines associations between UI and mental health outcomes without any intervention or control arms.
This is a review chapter on pathophysiology and drug therapy targets, not a primary randomised controlled trial. No intervention comparison or randomisation is described.
This is a review article discussing existing RCTs on PFMT regimens, not a primary randomised controlled trial. The stated aim is to 'review the present evidence' and discuss literature.
This describes functional electrical stimulation for bladder dysfunction but is not a randomised controlled trial. No randomisation or control arm is mentioned.
This is a secondary analysis of data from healthy women (N=38), not women with urinary incontinence. It is not a randomised controlled trial with intervention and control arms.
This is a methodological guidance document on preparing Summary of Findings tables, not a randomised controlled trial. No patient data or interventions are studied.
This is a methodological guidance document on presenting continuous outcomes in systematic reviews, not a randomised controlled trial.
This is a cross-sectional epidemiological survey assessing prevalence of UI in Norway, not a randomised controlled trial. No intervention or control arms exist.
This is a consensus-based terminology report, not a randomised controlled trial. It describes development of definitions through expert consensus.
This is a methodological paper about systematic reviews, not a primary randomised controlled trial. The abstract is very brief and indicates this is about review methodology.
This is a cross-sectional study using the Sickness Impact Profile questionnaire. Women were randomly selected from a clinic but this is not a randomised controlled trial with intervention arms.
This is a systematic review and economic modelling study, not a primary randomised controlled trial. It analyses 88 RCTs but is not itself an RCT.
This is a questionnaire development and validation study, not a randomised controlled trial. It assesses psychometric properties of a new instrument.
This is an economic study measuring willingness to pay, not a randomised controlled trial. It uses a questionnaire with binary willingness-to-pay questions.
This is a cross-sectional analysis using multivariate logistic regression from a national survey, not a randomised controlled trial. No intervention or control arms.
This is a questionnaire development and validation study, not a randomised controlled trial. It tests validity and reliability of a new QoL instrument.

While participants were from a 25-week longitudinal randomized control study, this paper focuses on validating the YIPS questionnaire, not testing PFMT vs no treatment. The intervention was a 'behavioral/educational intervention' which may not be PFMT, and the primary aim is psychometric validation.
This is a questionnaire validation study assessing content validity of the KHQ, not a randomised controlled trial. No intervention comparison is made.
This is a methodological study examining how trial quality affects meta-analysis results, not a primary randomised controlled trial. It analyses 127 existing RCTs from other meta-analyses.
This is a guidelines document for reporting RCTs, not a randomised controlled trial itself. No patient data or interventions are studied.
This is a cross-sectional survey assessing bothersomeness and QoL impact of UI, not a randomised controlled trial. No intervention or control arms.
This study involves healthy continent nulliparous women, not women with urinary incontinence. It is not a randomised controlled trial with intervention and control arms.
This is a methodological study developing and validating a severity index for UI, not a randomised controlled trial. It compares questionnaire-based index with pad-weighing tests.
This is a cross-sectional study comparing incontinent women with controls using the FSFI questionnaire, not a randomised controlled trial. No intervention or randomisation is described.

This is a prospective cohort study, not a randomised controlled trial. The study design does not meet the selection criteria which require RCTs or quasi-RCTs. The study focuses on validating a self-efficacy index rather than testing PFMT intervention.
This is an instrument development/validation study describing short forms of questionnaires. It is not a randomised controlled trial and does not test PFMT intervention.
This is a psychometric validation study developing a new quality of life measure (I-QOL). It is not a randomised controlled trial testing PFMT intervention.
This study validates a quality of life scale in patients with psoriasis, not urinary incontinence. The population does not match the review criteria (women with SUI/UUI/MUI). It is also not an RCT.

This is a secondary analysis validating global impression questionnaires using data from duloxetine trials. It is not a primary RCT comparing PFMT to inactive control. The intervention is duloxetine, not PFMT.
This is a scale development study for anxiety and depression in hospital settings. It does not involve urinary incontinence, PFMT, or RCT design.

This is a randomised controlled trial in women with stress urinary incontinence. The intervention group received pelvic floor muscle exercise training. There is a control group (n=27). The study meets all selection criteria: RCT design, women with SUI, PFMT intervention, and control arm.

This is a randomised study in women with stress urinary incontinence (IUE). Three groups: electrotherapy + exercises, exercises alone, and control (GC, n=22). The exercises group (PFMT) can be compared to the control group. Meets selection criteria: RCT, women with SUI, PFMT arm, and inactive control arm.

This is an RCT in women with urodynamic stress incontinence, but the intervention is acupressure, not pelvic floor muscle training. The study compares acupressure to sham and usual care. Does not meet criteria as there is no PFMT arm.

This RCT compares supervised pelvic floor exercise program (SEP) to home prescribed exercise program (HEP). Both arms involve active PFMT treatment. There is no no-treatment, placebo, sham or inactive control arm. Does not meet selection criteria.

This is a randomised controlled trial in women with SUI with 4 arms: combined treatment (PFMT+duloxetine), no active treatment (n=47), PFMT only (n=50), and duloxetine only (n=52). The PFMT-only arm can be compared to the no active treatment arm. Meets all selection criteria: RCT, women with SUI, PFMT arm, and inactive control arm.
This is a qualitative study using telephone interviews to explore women's experiences. It is not a randomised controlled trial. The study design does not meet selection criteria.

This is a secondary analysis examining predictors of success from a previous RCT. It uses logistic regression on follow-up data and is not itself a randomised controlled trial. Does not meet selection criteria.
This is a systematic review evaluating the effects of adding PFMT to other active treatments. It is not a primary randomised controlled trial. Does not meet selection criteria.

This is a review article providing an overview of exercise science related to PFM strength training. It compiles 16 articles but is not itself a randomised controlled trial. Does not meet selection criteria.
This is an anatomical/physiological review article describing urethrovesical structure. It is not a randomised controlled trial testing PFMT intervention. Does not meet selection criteria.
This is a scale validation study for psychiatric symptoms (somatization, anxiety, depression). It does not involve urinary incontinence, PFMT, or RCT design. Does not meet selection criteria.
This is a review chapter covering conservative management approaches for UI/POP. It is not a primary randomised controlled trial. Does not meet selection criteria.
This is a methodological paper about intention-to-treat principles in clinical trials. It is not an RCT testing PFMT for urinary incontinence. Does not meet selection criteria.
This is a systematic review (Cochrane review) comparing PFMT to other active treatments. It is not a primary randomised controlled trial. Does not meet selection criteria.
This is a consensus/methodological paper offering guidance on outcome measurements. It is not a randomised controlled trial testing PFMT intervention. Does not meet selection criteria.
This is an observational cohort study using MRI to compare pelvic floor morphology. It is not a randomised controlled trial testing PFMT intervention. Does not meet selection criteria.

This is an RCT, but it compares conservative treatment with prior urodynamics vs without prior urodynamics. Both arms receive active treatment (physiotherapy and bladder retraining). There is no no-treatment, placebo, sham or inactive control arm. Does not meet selection criteria.

This is an observational cohort study examining the causes of incontinence in institutionalized elderly. It is not a randomised controlled trial testing PFMT intervention. Does not meet selection criteria.
This is a systematic review (Cochrane review) on PFMT for antenatal/postnatal women. It is not a primary randomised controlled trial. Does not meet selection criteria.
